name: Hotel Original Vinayaka Mylari
why_it_matters: The original home of the Mylari dosa — a soft, cotton-textured, butter-laden take on the Mysore masala dosa, served here since 1938 from a recipe of founder Gowramma. A tiny six-table eatery in a lane near Nazarbad police station with only about five items on the menu; it has no branches despite the many imitator 'Mylari' hotels across the city. The single most-cited dosa address in Mysore.
insider_tip: Look for the green sign reading 'The Old Original Vinayaka Mylari' in red, next to Giri Stationery. Hours are 6.30am-1.30pm and 3-9pm — it closes over lunch. Six tables only, so expect to wait and share elbow room; the dosa comes with a dollop of white butter and saagu. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: Hotel Original Vinayaka Mylari, 769 Nazarbad Main Road, near Police Station, Mysuru, Karnataka 570010

name: Guru Sweet Mart
area: Sayyaji Rao Road, Devaraja Mohalla, Mysore
why_it_matters: A 100-square-foot shop on Sayyaji Rao Road near K.R. Circle, run by descendants of Kakasura Madappa — the royal cook who is credited with inventing Mysore Pak in the 19th-century kitchen of Maharaja Mummadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar. Opened as Guru Sweet Mart in 1957, it is widely regarded as the original home of the city's signature ghee-and-gram-flour sweet.
insider_tip: The shop is tiny and famous, so it gets crowded — buy the ghee Mysore Pak fresh and warm, when it is at its melt-in-the-mouth best. It is a takeaway sweet counter, not a sit-down restaurant. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: Guru Sweet Mart, Shop No. 1, Devaraja Market Building, Sayyaji Rao Road, near K.R. Circle, Devaraja Mohalla, Mysuru, Karnataka 570001

name: Hotel RRR Restaurant
why_it_matters: Mysore's go-to address for Andhra food — at Gandhi Square, serving fiery Andhra meals on banana leaf and spicy Andhra-style chicken and mutton biryanis. A long queue at lunch is the norm; reviewers repeatedly call its banana-leaf thali one of the best in the city.
insider_tip: Always packed and congested at lunch — go before 12.30pm or expect a wait. The veg meal is unlimited South Indian on a leaf with a mound of rice, sambar, rasam, veg, papad and pickle; non-veg diners go for the chicken biryani and chicken roast. Cash, UPI and cards.
signature_address: Hotel RRR Restaurant, Gandhi Square, Mysuru, Karnataka 570001

name: Hotel Hanumanthu
why_it_matters: Established in 1930 by chef Hanumanthappa on Akbar Road in Mandi Mohalla — the city's reference address for Mysore-style mutton pulav. The meat is freshly butchered and cooked with rice and home-ground spices over a wood fire, tender enough that locals describe it as melt-in-the-mouth, and served on dry plantain leaves.
insider_tip: There are four or five 'Hanumanthu' hotels on the same street — the original is at #1720 Akbar Road, opposite the Venus Egg Centre. It gets crowded after 12pm, so go early. Pulav is the order, not biryani. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: Hotel Hanumanthu, #1720 Akbar Road, opposite Venus Egg Centre, Mandi Mohalla, Mysuru, Karnataka 570001

name: Mahesh Prasad
signature_dish: Benne masala dosa with filter coffee
why_it_matters: A much-loved pure-veg South Indian restaurant in Mysore with a fiercely loyal customer base — people travel across the city for its crisp benne masala dosa, sambar and filter coffee. Reviewers also single out the bonda soup and rava idli as dishes hard to find done this well elsewhere.
insider_tip: Go for breakfast for the freshest dosa batch — the benne masala dosa and bonda soup are the orders, finished with the filter coffee. Reasonably priced, typical South Indian setting. Cash and UPI.

name: Sri Gayatri Tiffin Room (GTR)
why_it_matters: Known across the city simply as GTR, this humble pure-veg tiffin room in Chamundipuram has a cult following for what many locals rate among the best masala dosas in Mysore — fresh, consistent South Indian breakfast served every day.
insider_tip: Open 7am-3.30pm and 3.30-8pm, closed Mondays. The masala dosa is the order; go early for breakfast when the queue is shorter and the batch is freshest. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: Sri Gayatri Tiffin Room, Chamundipuram, Mysuru, Karnataka 570004

name: Indra Cafe's Paras
signature_dish: South Indian tiffin with filter coffee
why_it_matters: One of Mysore's legendary old eateries — a casual pure-veg cafe on Sayyaji Rao Road opposite Devaraja Market, established in 1956 by Sri Badri Prasad. Generations of Mysoreans associate childhood memories with its dosas, sweets and strong filter coffee.
insider_tip: Lively and popular, it can get crowded and service varies — come for the South Indian tiffin and the filter coffee. Handy to combine with a Devaraja Market walk across the road. Cash, UPI and cards.
signature_address: Indra Cafe's Paras, 1740 Sayyaji Rao Road, opposite Devaraja Market, Mysuru, Karnataka 570001

name: Bombay Tiffanys
why_it_matters: A long-running Mysore sweet shop on Sayyaji Rao Road — one of the city's most-cited names for sweets, drawing visitors for Mysore Pak and its range of traditional Karnataka mithai. A standard stop on the Sayyaji Rao Road sweets trail alongside Guru Sweet Mart.
insider_tip: Primarily a takeaway sweet counter — buy boxes of Mysore Pak or durbar laddu to carry home. Sayyaji Rao Road is the city's sweets street, so it is easy to compare a couple of shops. Cash, UPI and cards.
signature_address: Bombay Tiffanys, Sayyaji Rao Road, Mysuru, Karnataka 570001
